title: Contributing to TOP
text: Contributions improve statistical reliability, portability, performance, documentation, analyst usability welcome.

title: Contributing to TOP
text: Open issue changes alter statistical behavior public API. Work focused branch based master. Add reproducible test using simulated package data. Update relevant help page vignette. Run R CMD build . followed R CMD check TOP_*.tar.gz. Please include participant-level otherwise sensitive study data.

title: Contributing to TOP
text: top_*() functions recommended API. Existing exported functions retained backward compatibility. change estimates, tests, convergence, missing-data handling, subtype filtering must called explicitly supported regression tests.

title: Contributing to TOP
text: Native routines must registered, callable R API, must never call exit(), write directly stdout/stderr, use unregistered symbols.

title: Contributing to TOP
text: Include operating system, R version, TOP version, minimal example, sessionInfo() reporting failure.

title: Security and privacy
text: TOP statistical software receive participant-level data public issues, pull requests, example repositories. vulnerability expose data, corrupt results silently, crash R session, email andrew.haoyu@gmail.com opening public issue. Include TOP version, R version, operating system, synthetic reproducer possible. maintainer acknowledge report coordinate fix disclosure timeline.

title: Getting started with TOP
text: outcome matrix case-control status first column (0 controls 1 cases) tumor characteristics remaining columns. Tumor characteristics must NA controls. case tumor characteristics can missing, use distinct numeric code pass missing_value. simulated package data use 888 missing case tumor characteristics.
code: library(TOP) data("data", package = "TOP")  y <- data[, 1:5] snp <- data[, 6, drop = FALSE] pc1 <- data[, 7, drop = FALSE]  head(y) #>      case.control ER PR HER2 grade #> [1,]            0 NA NA   NA    NA #> [2,]            0 NA NA   NA    NA #> [3,]            1  1  0    1     1 #> [4,]            1  1  1  888   888 #> [5,]            1  1  1    0     0 #> [6,]            0 NA NA   NA    NA table(y[, 1]) #>  #>    0    1  #> 4888 5112

title: Getting started with TOP
text: Covariates can assigned different structures: baseline: common association across subtypes; additive: baseline plus tumor-marker main effects; pairwise: additive effects plus pairwise marker interactions; saturated: separate effect every retained subtype. example, common SNP effect can adjusted additive PC effect.
code: fit_mixed <- top_fit(   y = y,   baseline = snp,   additive = pc1,   missing_value = 888 )

title: Getting started with TOP
text: TOP historically omits subtypes counts cutoff. default subtype_cutoff = 10 preserves behavior. Lower cutoffs can make information matrices unstable, particularly small datasets. Numerical failures raise R errors instead terminating R session. Set options(TOP.verbose = TRUE) temporarily EM progress messages useful.

title: Getting started with TOP
text: TwoStageModel() remains available backward compatibility. New code prefer top_fit() named components fit$second.stage.test rather positional indexing.

title: Score-statistic meta-analysis
text: study supplies list : score: numeric score vector; information: corresponding square symmetric information matrix. studies must use parameter order second-stage design. combined score information sums across studies. TOP evaluates quadratic score statistic using combined information matrix.
code: library(TOP)  studies <- list(   array_a = list(     score = c(1.0, 2.0),     information = diag(c(2, 3))   ),   array_b = list(     score = c(0.5, -0.5),     information = diag(c(1, 2))   ),   array_c = list(     score = c(-0.25, 1.0),     information = diag(c(4, 1))   ) )  meta <- top_meta(studies) meta #> TOP score meta-analysis #> Studies: 3  #> Chi-squared: 1.2649 on 2 df; p = 0.5313 meta$score #> [1] 1.25 2.50 meta$information #>      [,1] [,2] #> [1,]    7    0 #> [2,]    0    6 meta$statistic #> [1] 1.264881 meta$p.value #> [1] 0.5312936

title: Score-statistic meta-analysis
text: top_meta() rejects non-finite scores, non-square asymmetric information matrices, inconsistent parameter dimensions, singular combined information matrix. Align parameter names allele coding constructing list; study-specific column mapping belongs analysis project rather package. ScoreMetaAnalysis() remains available older two-study scripts, new code use top_meta().

title: Score scans and detailed follow-up
text: top_score_support() fits null model containing adjustment covariates. returned object can reused every batch subjects, outcomes, nuisance model.
code: support <- top_score_support(   y = y,   additive = adjustment,   missing_value = 888 )  support #> TOP score-scan support #> Observations: 10000  Retained subtypes: 21  #> Dropped observations: 11

title: Score scans and detailed follow-up
text: variant column tested independently. default additive structure tests baseline effect tumor-marker main effects jointly. genome-wide data, pass manageable column batches reusing support. Singular information matrices recorded status column NA p-value, allowing batch scan continue.
code: scan <- top_score_scan(   y = y,   variants = variants,   support = support,   structure = "additive",   missing_value = 888 )  as.data.frame(scan) #>   variant statistic df    p.value status #> 1     SNP  10.91802  5 0.05302981     ok scan$score #>     baseline effect ER main effect PR main effect HER2 main effect #> SNP        57.47495       46.01162        37.4334         53.06665 #>     grade main effect #> SNP          107.4106 all_results <- lapply(variant_batches, function(batch) {   as.data.frame(top_score_scan(     y = y,     variants = batch,     support = support,     missing_value = 888   )) }) all_results <- do.call(rbind, all_results)

title: Score scans and detailed follow-up
text: top_followup() fits one detailed Wald model per selected variant extracts variant-specific global association, global heterogeneity, second-stage effect results. Use on_error = "record" (default) several selected variants single nonconvergent model reported without discarding successful fits. Use keep_models = TRUE full fitted top_model objects needed.
code: followup <- top_followup(   y = y,   variants = variants,   adjustment = adjustment,   variant_structure = "additive",   missing_value = 888,   keep_models = FALSE )  followup$results #>   variant global_association_p global_heterogeneity_p status #> 1     SNP               0.0543                  0.126     ok followup$effects #>   Covariate SecondStageEffect OddsRatio OddsRatio(95%CI low) #> 1       SNP   baseline effect      0.90                 0.76 #> 2       SNP    ER main effect      0.95                 0.85 #> 3       SNP    PR main effect      1.05                 0.93 #> 4       SNP  HER2 main effect      1.16                 1.01 #> 5       SNP grade main effect      1.08                 1.01 #>   OddsRatio(95%CI high) Pvalue #> 1                  1.07 0.2390 #> 2                  1.08 0.4550 #> 3                  1.19 0.4490 #> 4                  1.35 0.0400 #> 5                  1.17 0.0368

title: TOP: Two-Stage Polytomous Logistic Regression
text: TOP fits two-stage polytomous logistic regression models case-control studies multiple disease tumor characteristics. supports missing tumor-marker data, reusable fixed-effect score scans, detailed variant follow-, custom subtype designs, score-statistic meta-analysis.

title: TOP: Two-Stage Polytomous Logistic Regression
text: Install development release GitHub: load TOP:
code: install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("andrewhaoyu/TOP") library(TOP)

title: TOP: Two-Stage Polytomous Logistic Regression
text: outcome matrix contains case-control status column 1 tumor characteristics remaining columns. Controls must NA tumor characteristics. package example, 888 marks missing tumor data among cases. TOP model results stable names standard methods:
code: data("data", package = "TOP")  y <- data[, 1:5] snp <- data[, 6, drop = FALSE] pc1 <- data[, 7, drop = FALSE]  fit <- top_fit(   y = y,   additive = cbind(snp, pc1),   missing_value = 888 )  fit fit$second.stage.test fit$global.test summary(fit) coef(fit, stage = "second") vcov(fit, stage = "second")

title: TOP: Two-Stage Polytomous Logistic Regression
text: Fit nuisance model reuse across variant batches: Fit detailed Wald models selected variants:
code: support <- top_score_support(   y = y,   additive = pc1,   missing_value = 888 )  scan <- top_score_scan(   y = y,   variants = snp,   support = support,   missing_value = 888 )  as.data.frame(scan) followup <- top_followup(   y = y,   variants = snp,   adjustment = pc1,   missing_value = 888,   keep_models = FALSE )  followup$results followup$effects

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ data(data, package="TOP") #load in the breast cancer example #this is a simulated breast cancer example #there are around 5000 breast cancer cases and 5000 controls, i.e. people without disease data[1:5,]  #four different tumor characteristics were included, ER (positive vs negative), PR (positive vs negative), HER2 (positive vs negative), grade (ordinal 1, 2, 3) #the phenotype file y <- data[,1:5]  #one SNP and one Principal components (PC1) are the covariates SNP <- data[,6,drop=FALSE] PC1 <- data[,7,drop=FALSE]  #fit the additive two-stage model model.1 <- TwoStageModel(y=y,additive=cbind(SNP,PC1),                          missingTumorIndicator = 888)                           #the second stage odds ratio (95% CI) and p-value.  #the baseline effect is the case-control odds ratio of the reference subtype (ER-,PR-,HER2-,grade0).  #The main effect are the case-case odds ratio of the tumor characteristics. model.1[[4]]   #the global association test and global heterogeneity test result of the covariates. model.1[[5]]   model.1[[7]] #the case-control odds ratios for all of the subtypes.  #instead of additive model, you can also try different combinations. # For example, for the PC1, we use the additive model,  #but for SNP, we use the baseline only model. model.2 <- TwoStageModel(y=y,baselineonly = SNP,                       additive=PC1,                       missingTumorIndicator = 888) } # }
